title: Closed pushforward preserves and reflects relative module flatness
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Closed immersions are representable and become closed immersions of schemes on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Modules are on the small etale ringed sites, with quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $T$ be an $S$-scheme, $f:X\to T$ a morphism, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion, and $G$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module. Relative flatness of a quasi-coherent module on $X$ or $Z$ means that on every etale scheme chart $U$ its Zariski stalk at $u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t(u)}$, as in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Then $G$ is flat over $T$ through $f\circ i$ if and only if $i_*G$ is flat over $T$ through $f$. In particular $Z\to T$ is flat in the chartwise sense [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] if and only if $i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is flat over $T$. Neither $i$ nor $f$ is assumed flat or of finite presentation, and no Noetherian assumption is imposed.

Relative-flatness assertion stated from the etale-chart/closed-pushforward stalk argument.

proof.text: Put $F=i_*G$. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules], $F$ is quasi-coherent, without finiteness hypotheses. For any etale scheme chart $a:U\to X$, put $V=Z\times_XU$ and $j:V\hookrightarrow U$. This is a closed immersion of schemes by the representability convention [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The restriction formula [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] identifies $F|_U$ with $j_*(G|_V)$ on small etale sites. Let $H$ be the Zariski quasi-coherent module corresponding to $G|_V$. The equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies the Zariski module corresponding to $F|_U$ with $j_*H$. More explicitly, use the unrestricted first clause of [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square]: restriction of small etale direct image to Zariski opens is Zariski direct image, identically on sections. Thus no general base-change theorem or extra finiteness condition is needed here. We will compute ordinary Zariski stalks, not geometric stalks.

For the scheme closed immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow U$, identify $|V|$ with its closed image. Apply [lem-sc-closed-pushforward-abelian-stalks] to the underlying abelian sheaf of $H$. At $u\notin j(V)$ the stalk $(j_*H)_u$ is zero. At $u=j(v)$ the comparison $(j_*H)_u\simeq H_v$ sends the germ of a section on $W\subseteq U$ to its germ on $j^{-1}W$. This is linear over $\mathcal O_{T,f(a(u))}$: a germ of a base function acts on both sections by its pullback through the same composite $V\to U\to X\to T$, so the germ map commutes with this action. Therefore these are identifications of modules over the actual base Zariski local ring. The zero module is flat since tensoring with it sends any injection to $0\to0$. By the stalk criterion [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], $F|_U$ is flat over $T$ if and only if $G|_V$ is flat over $T$.

Suppose $G$ is flat over $T$ in the stipulated chartwise sense. For every $U\to X$ as in Step 1, $V\to Z$ is an etale scheme chart, so $G|_V$ is flat over $T$. Step 2 then gives flatness of $F|_U$. Quantifying over all these $U$ is exactly flatness of $F$ over $T$. This uses no flatness of $i$ or $f$.

source.place: Tag 0D00 (lemma-hilb-is-quot), omitted forward flatness argument expanded using Steps 1 and 2

proof.text: Conversely suppose $F$ is flat over $T$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to X$, which exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space], and put $V=Z\times_XU$. Then $V$ is a scheme and $V\to Z$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Step 2 implies that $G|_V$ is flat over $T$. To check the definition on an arbitrary etale scheme chart $W\to Z$, form $E=W\times_ZV$. This is a scheme; $E\to W$ is surjective etale and $E\to V$ is etale by the same fibre-product statement. Etale scheme maps are flat [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The pullback compatibility of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies the Zariski module on $E$ both with the pullback of the one on $V$ and with the pullback of the one on $W$. Apply [lem-trf-relative-flatness-source-cover] first to $E\to V$: its pointwise forward implication proves flatness over $T$ on $E$. Apply its surjective-flat converse to $E\to W$: flatness over $T$ descends to $W$. Since $W$ was arbitrary, $G$ is flat over $T$.

source.place: Tag 02JZ (lemma-flat-permanence); descent.tex Tags 03DX and 03LC (1); quot.tex Tag 0D00 reverse flatness implication

proof.text: Apply the equivalence to $G=\mathcal O_Z$, which is quasi-coherent (it has its one-generator free presentation). It remains to compare the two stated flatness conventions. For a scheme chart $W\to Z$, flatness of its structure module over $T$ says exactly that $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ for every $w$, which is flatness of $W\to T$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The chart test [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] includes the target chart $T\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}T$, so chartwise flatness of $Z\to T$ implies these conditions. Conversely, for any target etale chart $B\to T$ and any diagram $W\to B$ over $Z\to T$, apply [lem-trf-etale-local-ring-flatness] to the $\mathcal O_{B,b}$-module $\mathcal O_{W,w}$. It is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ if and only if it is flat over $\mathcal O_{B,b}$. Thus all the scheme maps $W\to B$ in the chart test are flat. This proves precisely that $Z\to T$ is flat if and only if $\mathcal O_Z$ is flat over $T$, and the claimed particular case follows.
